description:
Data Standardizer provides implementations of various internationally recognised standards in data processing, covering topics ranging from languages to currencies and geographical entities. With strongly-typed enumerations for each standard (where applicable) or other targeted data types, you can represent these elements in your code such that errors with invalid values are minimised.

Provides types supporting the measurement and comparison of date and time periods, including:
- TZ Database
- Unix time
- DOS date/time
releaseNotes:
- Add TZ Database zone line, rule and offset model types.
- Add the public types that describe the TZ Database zone lines and daylight saving rules generated from the source, and the offsets and transitions calculated from them.
- TzDataZoneLine and TzDataRule are immutable classes corresponding to the Zone and Rule lines of the source, and TzDataUntil, TzDataOffsetInfo and TzDataTransition are readonly structs with value equality.
- Every constructor is internal, so that only generated data can create an instance, and each validates its arguments: a day specification must be consistent with its kind, a zone line's rules and fixed save must agree with its rule kind, and every instant on an offset or transition must be a universal time.
- TzDataRule.GetTransitionDate resolves the date of a rule's transition in a given year.
- A rule keeps the name of its rule set for diagnostics, but internally, since the tz project does not treat rule names as stable.
- Expose the internals of Chronology to its tests, which cover every day kind across month ends, year ends and leap years, the argument validation of each type, and the absence of public constructors and of ValueTuple from the public API.
- Compare the constructor arguments of the TZ Database model types with null through the is pattern rather than the equality operator, which a type may overload and the pattern cannot invoke.
- Generate TZ Database zone lines and rule sets as TzDataTimezone members.
- Parse the main-format region files of the TZ Database at generation time, and generate the full zone line history of every timezone, with the rule sets it references, as members of TzDataTimezone.
- The new TzDataParser module tokenises the africa, antarctica, asia, australasia, europe, northamerica and southamerica files, discarding comments and gathering Zone continuation lines, and converts their columns as zic does.
- The generator now writes two partial files beside the main one, which still goes to the output stream: TzDataTimezone.ZoneLineData.cs, with an array of zone lines per timezone, and TzDataTimezone.RuleSets.cs, with an array of rules per referenced rule set.
- The post-generation edits once made by hand are now made by the script: the struct is readonly, the nested classes are static, and the nullable context follows the auto-generated header.
- The zone line array is held in a field declared beside the identifier, since the order of fields split across partial declarations is undefined.
- Equality, hashing, comparison, ToString and IConvertible continue to use the identifier only.
- Tests cover every timezone field: each has zone lines, only the last without an UNTIL, UNTIL values that strictly increase, and rules for every line that references a rule set.
- Update TZ Database to version 2026e.
- America/Winnipeg and America/Inuvik gain zone lines for the move of Manitoba and the western Northwest Territories to permanent standard time from late 2026, and their comments now read "EST - Manitoba, ON (northwest)" and "CST - NT (west)".
- Other Canadian zones that observed a fixed save in late 2026 now follow the Canada rule set until then.
- Historical corrections: Colombia's 1992 transition moves to May 2, Iran's 1979 transition is at 0:00, Europe/Dublin gains 1925 zone lines, and the Alaska purchase transitions of 1867 are given in universal time.
- Calculate UTC offsets, DST state and transitions for TzDataTimezone.
- Calculate the offset from universal time in effect in any timezone at any instant, from its zone lines and rules, and the transitions between offsets over any period.
- The internal TzDataZoneCalculator follows the outzone function of zic.
- Transitions are precomputed up to the last year for which the zone has explicit data.
- A DateTime argument of kind Unspecified is treated as universal time, and one of kind Local throws ArgumentException.
- The abbreviation in each offset is formatted from the zone line's FORMAT as zic formats it, with %s, %z and the standard/daylight slash form.
- The existing attribute lookup of TzDataExtensions now finds the timezone field in the shared registry, rather than reflecting over every field on each call.
- Every transition of every timezone from 1800 to 2150 matches the output of zdump -v for TZ Database 2026e, compiled by zic.
- Closes.
- Format TZ Database zone abbreviations, including standard and daylight variants.
- Add TzDataExtensions methods that give the abbreviation of a timezone at an instant, and its standard time and daylight saving time variants, each with a DateTime and a DateTimeOffset overload: GetAbbreviation, GetStandardAbbreviation and GetDaylightAbbreviation.
- GetAbbreviation gives the abbreviation in force, as TzDataOffsetInfo does.
- A rule is in effect in a year where it takes effect in the year, or is in effect as the year begins, as war time was in New York throughout 1943.
- Tests cover EST/EDT, GMT/BST, AEST/AEDT, Dublin's IST/GMT, the %z forms of Dubai, Kathmandu and Lord Howe, Kolkata's IST, local mean time, war and peace time in New York from 1942 to 1946, British Standard Time, a fixed-save line, the time before the first rule, and the zone line boundary in Moscow; every timezone at both ends of the range of DateTime; and the argument and instance errors shared with the offset methods.
- Name the TZ Database offset test methods with nameof.
- Label the cases of the shared offset method test data with the nameof operator rather than string literals, so that the labels follow any rename of the methods they name.
- Expose TzDataTimezone location metadata as members and deprecate TzDataTimezoneAttribute.
- Add Latitude, Longitude, IsoCountryCodes and Comment properties to TzDataTimezone, giving callers a migration path before the attribute is removed in v2.0.
- The generator now passes each timezone's location metadata to the constructor of its field by named argument, beside the zone lines.
- The generator still applies TzDataTimezoneAttribute to every field, so callers that read it by reflection keep working, and suppresses CS0618 around the fields.
- TzDataTimezone.cs is regenerated from TZ Database 2026e, the release it was generated from, so the diff shows only the structural changes.
- Tests check, for every timezone field, that the members return the values of the attribute, and that a cast instance returns the values of the field.
- Add Parse, TryParse and IParsable to TzDataTimezone.
- Add a validating alternative to the explicit cast, which accepts any string.
- On .NET 7 and later, TzDataTimezone also implements IParsable<TzDataTimezone>, declared in the hand-written partial so the generator's base-type list is unchanged.
- Tests check, for every timezone field, that Parse and TryParse return the field with its zone lines, and cover unknown identifiers, null, and use through a generic IParsable<T> helper.
- Support TZ Database Link aliases in TzDataTimezone.
- Give each Link listed in zone.tab, such as Europe/Oslo, a field in the normal hierarchy.
- Add IsLink and Canonical to TzDataTimezone.
- The generator now reads zone.tab, etcetera and backward, resolves link chains transitively, and fails on a cycle, a chain that does not end at a Zone, or a zone.tab entry that is neither canonical nor a link.
- Tests cover every field's Canonical and shared zone lines array, sample zone.tab links and their locations, every deprecated link, cast instances, and the invalid instance errors.
